reviews.title: ⭐ 1/5 — Extremely Expensive Weekly Subscription and Difficult Cancellation
reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed with DramaWave’s subscription pricing and cancellation process.

My biggest concern is the ridiculously expensive weekly VIP subscription, costing approximately £14.93 per week. That is nearly £60 every four weeks and over £770 annually if continuously renewed!

I was charged £14.83 every week throughout October, totalling £59.32. What made the experience even more frustrating was how difficult it was to locate the cancellation option. I had to contact customer support and spend considerable time navigating the app before finally cancelling my subscription.

For an entertainment app offering short dramas, I find this pricing excessive and poor value for money.

Subscriptions should be reasonably priced, transparent and easy to cancel.

I strongly encourage other users to check the recurring charges carefully before subscribing.

My rating: 1 star. I would not recommend this subscription at its current price.

reviews.title: ⭐ 1/5 – Misleading and frustrating! Don’t waste your money.
reviews.text:
I discovered this app through an Instagram ad and got hooked on a story I genuinely wanted to finish.

The app showed 30 episodes, so I paid for VIP access, expecting to finally see how the story ends.

Only after paying did I discover that the story doesn’t actually have a proper ending! There’s no information about when the next episodes will be released, or even whether the story will continue.

You get people invested in a story, charge them to keep watching, and then leave them hanging with no answers.

If a series is unfinished, you should clearly disclose that BEFORE asking people to pay.

I feel misled, and I regret spending my money here. I want a refund.

Be transparent with your customers instead of making them pay for an unfinished experience!

reviews.title: App Function Review Only
reviews.text:
The functionality of the app needs reworked and improved. There needs to be advanced filtering options. There are many titles that I like to save to my list, but I haven’t watched yet. My list should not be combined with my watched history. The my list option should only show videos I’m interested in watching. and marked if they have been completed. I would like to see a filter or sort that shows incomplete videos. I don’t understand the ticket option. On all pages, it should show ones that I have already watched completely, and how many episodes I have watched of that particular video. There should also be a thumbs down or don’t recommend option. For example, I am not interested in same-sex lover stories. I do not want those types of stories to auto-play. 

I would also like the option of watching videos in landscape mode. Using this app on an iPad, is difficult to do when the case for my iPad is landscape only. For example, my iPad, case is the iPad Magic Keyboard.

It would also be helpful to be able to control the background music volume separately. In many cases, the background music is way too loud. Overpowering what is being said.

reviews.title: Ridiculous rip-off
reviews.text: At first, it’s easy to get hypnotized by the luscious visuals. But quickly, I was disillusioned by the huge holes in the stories, the poor quality of writing for the scripts, and the absolute thievery of this company. It’s easy to see what movies they copied, what faces they stole from celebrities, and what art they used without any payback to the artists. It is a totally unconscionable app, ripping people off. They don’t even check their stories for huge mistakes or even bother to make the characters look different. So many stories had multiple characters looking exactly the same. The app itself is fine, but the ads make it nearly unusable. Almost every ad I get has no visible way to close it after it finishes. It takes you to a screen prompting you to download another app, with no X or obvious way to return to DramaWave. I end up having to force-close DramaWave and reopen it just to continue watching.

I understand that a free app needs ads, and I don’t mind watching them, but users should always be able to close an ad once it has finished. I should not feel like I have to download another app just to get back to the content I was watching. Please fix the ad experience.

reviews.title: Silent charges, no receipts, no real support
reviews.text:
I was charged four times over a month and only discovered it when I read my credit card statement. No email receipt was sent for any of the charges, and the charges are timed overnight.
Because payment is processed by DramaWave rather than through the App Store, nothing appears in Apple purchase history, so there is no record on the Apple side to check against, and Apple’s refund flow doesn’t apply.
“Support” is an AI chat with preloaded questions. There is no path to a human, no ticket number, and no way to submit a cancellation or refund request that gets an actual answer.
A subscription service that bills without receipts and provides no reachable support should not be on the App Store. Check your card statement if you have ever subscribed here.

reviews.title: Length of reel to ad, autoplay/pause.
reviews.text:
This isn’t my first rodeo with reels and stories or (as I like to call them) audio books with pictures. I won’t name the one I like better but I’m use to watching a video and getting 3 to 5 minutes of extra watch time.

On DramaWave, you literally have to watch a 30 second ad for a 30 second clip. And you can watch up to 10-20 ads a day for 30 seconds clip per ad.

On the one I like, you are guaranteed 30mins free of a audio book that you can watch an animated/Ai generated video or just listen without the screen on while you’re doing other things and you also have the option of watching 10 ads which equates to an additional episode or 3-5mins of the series you want. You had the option to automatically play and use your coins to unlock the next episode or not so you can save your coins(again which is 3-5mins and sometimes up to 9mins each episode of what audio series varied).

I was so invested in my audiobook/ episodes that including the 10 ads per day, I spent at least $100 one year.

If the devs could make each reel 3mins at least while watching an ad, even if you don’t do the guaranteed 30mins free each day and make your stories/reels longer, and have the option to not automatically play what coins you have, I’d spend money on buying coins while also taking advantage of the 10-20 ads per day.

I get it, it’s a reel but watching a 30 seconds ad for a 30 seconds reel makes me think I’m cheated of my time and doesn’t make me want to buy coins especially without the option of

reviews.title: ⭐️1/5 Extremely frustrating experience
reviews.text:
DramaWave is one of the most poorly built subscription apps I’ve used. The whole payment and account system is confusing and incredibly vague.

I paid for a weekly VIP subscription after being asked to log in with my email. The payment went through, but somehow the subscription doesn’t show up on my account. When I log in with the same email, I still can’t access the movies I supposedly paid for. How does a paid subscription not properly connect to the account you just logged into?

There’s also no clear place to manage or cancel the subscription, which makes the whole thing feel extremely sketchy.

Customer service is another nightmare. It seems to be bots every time, with no clear way to reach an actual human. Responses take forever, if they respond at all.

If you’re going to charge people for a subscription, the absolute basics should work: payment confirmation, account syncing, access to paid content, subscription management, and actual customer support.

At this point, the entire experience feels like a scam. I would not recommend paying for DramaWave until they seriously fix their subscription system and customer service.

reviews.title: Mostly AI, increasingly p*rnographic
reviews.text: I like verticals and started watching DramaWave because I was curious about animated microdramas. DramaWave has a lot of them, and they use different genres than live-action (like fantasy, historical and Romantasy) which is cool…but the AI is distracting because it’s used too heavily. At least hire voice actors so the characters are speaking the words correctly. And several of their series are just playing out sexual fantasies (which mostly include sexual violence 🤢🤮), and the app recently released a tool to make them interactive. You can upload a photo to create an avatar that will be inserted as the protagonist of the vertical and you decide what the avatar does during steamy scenes. So the app is effectively allowing you to make your own erotica…which isn’t what I watch microdramas for. It also seems like this could be used for creepy purposes (you can upload any picture you want, and if it’s not a picture of you, then you’re making explicit material about someone who didn’t agree to it).

Extremely disappointing and a complete waste of money. I paid for a subscription expecting to watch dramas with real actors, only to find the app flooded with AI-generated content. The AI shows are low quality, lack genuine emotion, and feel nothing like the live-action dramas I subscribed for.

To make matters worse, there is no clear way to filter out AI content, so I spent more time searching for something watchable than actually watching anything. For a paid service, this is unacceptable. The app feels misleading, offers poor value for money, and seems more interested in filling the catalogue with cheap AI content than providing quality entertainment.

I will not be renewing my subscription and would not recommend this app to anyone looking for real-actor dramas. Save your money and look elsewhere.

They have to either lengthen the episodes or go back to 50 coins per episode throughout the series.

reviews.title: Violence wrapped up as entertainment
reviews.text:
I downloaded DramaWave expecting romance stories and escapism, but what I found was disturbing. A huge number of the storylines rely on abuse against women as “entertainment”. Female characters are constantly slapped, kicked, whipped, humiliated and tortured. There are repeated themes of fathers abusing daughters, ex-boyfriends assaulting women, and powerful male figures controlling or hurting female characters.

At some point you have to ask why so many “romances” are built around violence and degradation. Abuse is not romance. Watching women constantly suffer for drama value becomes exhausting and uncomfortable very quickly.

The app seems to normalise toxic and abusive behaviour instead of telling meaningful love stories. I understand conflict is part of drama, but there is a difference between storytelling and repeatedly using violence against women as a plot device.

Very disappointing and honestly unsettling.

reviews.title: Beware! A Hidden "Escalating Cost" Scam
reviews.text:
Dramawave is a predatory app that uses deceptive pricing to trap viewers. Unlike honest streaming services, they deliberately hide the true cost of a series until you are too invested to quit.
The Bait-and-Switch Pricing:
• Hidden Costs: They do not inform you of the total price to finish a story upfront. You enter thinking episodes are 60 coins, only to find the price increases to 90+ coins as you get closer to the finale.
• The "Sunk Cost" Trap: By the time the price hikes occur, you’ve already spent $10–$20. They bank on you paying the "inflated" rate rather than walking away from a story you’ve already paid half for.
• No Price Transparency: There is no way to see the coin requirements for later episodes. Your initial budget calculation is made irrelevant because the app changes the rules mid-stream.
• Poor Value: A single 90-minute story can end up costing over $50—triple the price of a monthly Netflix sub—for content that is often low-budget and repetitive.

Really disappointing considering they charge a whopping $40 per month, more than the rest of my subscriptions combined. I will say it’s addicting, but so are the Asian dramas on Netflix, and they are of much higher quality for a much lower monthly fee! Not sure what the developers are thinking.
